description: What core’s Prolog packs answer when they are loaded TOGETHER (PL.core-prolog-predicate-dups, U115). Each kb opens with the shipped packs verbatim and in order, comment and blank lines dropped: the combat pack (src/prolog/mechanics/combat-predicates.ts), npc-reasoning (src/prolog/npc-reasoning.ts) and ToTT (src/prolog/tott-predicates.ts) for the alive/1 cases, npc-reasoning and ToTT for the adult/1 and founding cases; the random_chance/1 cases load only the reference host rule. Regenerate with `npm run pack-agreement-corpus`. (1) alive/1 has one meaning, the fact: the character block’s or a playthrough’s, retracted by a death, and no pack defines a clause of it, so a living person is alive once, a target combat killed and a person whose death was recorded are not alive, and can_attack/2 and npc-reasoning’s readers agree. (2) adult/1, and every other life stage both packs used to state (child/1, adolescent/1, elderly/1, school_age/1, should_socialize/1), is defined once, in npc-reasoning, so adult/1 and should_found_business/1 yield each solution once. (3) random_chance/1 is one host-side seeded draw per call: a failed call has drawn, a call leaves no choice point, and a run replays under its seed. The reference stream is src/prolog/tott-predicates.ts RANDOM_CHANCE_REFERENCE_RULE (a linear congruential generator over ISO integer arithmetic; state random_chance_state/1), and every expected number is computed by nextRandomChanceState in TypeScript, not read back from an engine.
